title: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 17](/bible/joshua/17)

## Introduction

This session covers [Joshua 17](/bible/joshua/17) through 20 verse by verse: the lot of the tribe of Manasseh, the seven tribes still waiting for their inheritance and the lots cast at Shiloh, the portions of Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan, and the cities of refuge with the laws of the slayer. Bible maps of the conquest of the land of Canaan are used throughout to bring the scriptures to life, so we can see where our forefathers and foremothers, the real twelve tribes of Israel, lived in the land.

**[Joshua 17:1](/bible/joshua/17#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/17#v1)</sup> There was also a lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the firstborn of Joseph; to wit, for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead: because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

- A lot goes into an allotment, a portion; there was a portion for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.
- Bashan was the kingdom of Og, one of the giants that Israel conquered under Joshua. Before the conquest all this territory was called the land of Canaan, with the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites and their families dwelling in it.
- Prior to this chapter Judah received his inheritance in chapter 15 and the inheritance of Joseph, Ephraim, came in chapter 16; after the victories the Most High gave through Christ, the land was divided by lot so that every tribe had its portion.
- The Bible maps that even the enemies of Israel put together according to the scriptures show this history: Manasseh held Bashan and a portion by Gilead on the other side of Jordan. The so-called Cubans come from this tribe; this is their history that their enemies do not want them to know.

**[Joshua 17:2](/bible/joshua/17#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/17#v2)</sup> There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families; for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph by their families.

- There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph.
- Remember that Manasseh was the son of Joseph; Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.

**[Joshua 17:3-4](/bible/joshua/17#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/17#v3)</sup> But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/17#v4)</sup> And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren. Therefore according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

- Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
- They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying the Lord commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their brethren; and according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

**[Joshua 17:5-6](/bible/joshua/17#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/joshua/17#v5)</sup> And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side Jordan;
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/17#v6)</sup> Because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh’s sons had the land of Gilead.

- Ten portions fell to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan which were on the other side of Jordan. On the map the Jordan river flows down through the land, and across the river sat Gilead and Bashan, the lands Manasseh already held.
- Down south the Jordan empties into the Dead Sea, and Sodom and Gomorrah sat south of the Dead Sea, by where Edom was residing; the maps give a good feel for what the Bible is talking about.
- The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, just as the Lord commanded for the daughters of Zelophehad, and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.

**[Joshua 17:7-8](/bible/joshua/17#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/17#v7)</sup> And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of En–tappuah.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/17#v8)</sup> Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim;

- The coast of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethah; Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.
- We have to know where our forefathers came from and what the Bible is speaking about; that is why we search out these borders on the maps, where Tappuah sat on the southern border by Shechem.

**[Joshua 17:9-11](/bible/joshua/17#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/17#v9)</sup> And the coast descended unto the river Kanah, southward of the river: these cities of Ephraim are among the cities of Manasseh: the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea:
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/joshua/17#v10)</sup> Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border; and they met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/joshua/17#v11)</sup> And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth–shean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and her towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and her towns, even three countries.

- The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east.
- This land of Canaan is also known as Israel, and this is where our foremothers and forefathers lived: the so-called Mexicans, Guatemalans, and Hondurans lived here, and the so-called Brazilians, Colombians, and Venezuelans up in these coasts. A lot of times we read that Asher lived here and forget it is talking about us; our people need the visual.
- Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries.

**[Joshua 17:12-13](/bible/joshua/17#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/joshua/17#v12)</sup> Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/joshua/17#v13)</sup> Yet it came to pass, when the children of Israel were waxen strong, that they put the Canaanites to tribute; but did not utterly drive them out.

- Even though Israel conquered the majority of the land of Canaan, there were still areas the Canaanites kept possession of; the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
- When the children of Israel were waxen strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out; they kept them as servants and handmaids.

**[Joshua 17:14-15](/bible/joshua/17#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/17#v14)</sup> And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to inherit, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the Lord hath blessed me hitherto?
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/17#v15)</sup> And Joshua answered them, If thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee.

- The children of Joseph, led by Ephraim, asked Joshua why he gave them but one lot to inherit, seeing they are a great people; great here means numerous. Ephraim and Manasseh were among the most populated tribes, and Ephraim's own portion had already been given back in chapter 16.
- Their fruitfulness was prophesied when Israel blessed Joseph; the very name Ephraim goes into being fruitful.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 49:22](/bible/genesis/49#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/genesis/49#v22)</sup> Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall:

    Joseph is a fruitful bough; the fruitfulness of Joseph's seed was prophesied by Israel.

- Joshua answered without bias: if thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, into the forest, and cut down there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee. Narrow means too small: if you are complaining that your lot is too small, then go to war and conquer more land.

**[Joshua 17:16](/bible/joshua/17#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/joshua/17#v16)</sup> And the children of Joseph said, The hill is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are of Beth–shean and her towns, and they who are of the valley of Jezreel.

- The children of Joseph answered that the hill is not enough for them, and the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron; those nations had military power too.
- On the map those Canaanites sat right north of Manasseh, in Beth-shean and her towns and in the valley of Jezreel, dwelling in the midst of our brothers with an army; they were a problem, and Manasseh was already having a hard time with them.

**[Joshua 17:17-18](/bible/joshua/17#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/joshua/17#v17)</sup> And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great power: thou shalt not have one lot only:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/joshua/17#v18)</sup> But the mountain shall be thine; for it is a wood, and thou shalt cut it down: and the outgoings of it shall be thine: for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, and though they be strong.

- Joshua told the house of Joseph, thou art a great people and hast great power; the mountain shall be thine, and thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they be strong. Going through the wood means going through the dense forest; it would be a struggle, but at the end of the day they would overcome.
- Manasseh had issues driving the Canaanites out, but Ephraim did it. The difference between the two brothers goes back to [Genesis 48](/bible/genesis/48), where Israel blessed Joseph's sons and crossed his hands, guiding them wittingly, meaning he knew exactly what he was doing.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 48:1-2](/bible/genesis/48#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/genesis/48#v1)</sup> And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/48#v2)</sup> And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh unto thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.

    Joseph brought his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim to his sick father, and Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed, glad to see his son.
  - **[Genesis 48:8-11](/bible/genesis/48#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/genesis/48#v8)</sup> And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who are these?
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/genesis/48#v9)</sup> And Joseph said unto his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/48#v10)</sup> Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/genesis/48#v11)</sup> And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed.

    Israel's eyes were dim for age; he kissed and embraced Joseph's sons, saying he had not thought to see Joseph's face, and lo, God had shewed him his seed also.
  - **[Genesis 48:12-14](/bible/genesis/48#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/genesis/48#v12)</sup> And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/genesis/48#v13)</sup> And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near unto him.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/genesis/48#v14)</sup> And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn.

    Joseph set Manasseh toward Israel's right hand for the greater blessing of the firstborn, but Israel stretched his right hand upon Ephraim the younger, guiding his hands wittingly.
  - **[Genesis 48:17-19](/bible/genesis/48#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/genesis/48#v17)</sup> And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head unto Manasseh’s head.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/genesis/48#v18)</sup> And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/genesis/48#v19)</sup> And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.

    It displeased Joseph and he held up his father's hand, but Israel refused, saying I know it, my son: Manasseh shall also be great, but his younger brother shall be greater, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.

- Ephraim being greater goes into Ephraim becoming the head of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria; and it was Ephraim that led the charge, with the help of Issachar and Manasseh, that brought the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. The unicorn there is not a fairy tale horse; the original etymology goes into the rhinoceros.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 33:17](/bible/deuteronomy/33#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/33#v17)</sup> His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of unicorns: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.

    Joseph's horns are the horns of unicorns, and with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth; they are the ten thousands of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh.
  - **[Isaiah 7:9](/bible/isaiah/7#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/7#v9)</sup> And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

    The head of Ephraim is Samaria; Ephraim became the ruler of the ten tribes.
  - **[Judges 8:1](/bible/judges/8#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/judges/8#v1)</sup> And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply.

    The men of Ephraim chided sharply with Gideon for not calling them to the battle against the Midianites; that war-like spirit was always in Ephraim.

- The Zondervan compact Bible dictionary, a tool to add to your arsenal, says Ephraim and Manasseh seem to have been bitter rivals, Manasseh being the larger group, but Ephraim asserting the more vigorous leadership, though they seem to have held their land in common for a time. Vigorous means very passionate, sometimes rough; that is the spirit the children of Ephraim have.
- In [Judges 7](/bible/judges/7) Manasseh went to war with the three hundred men and destroyed the Midianites though they were lower in numbers, because Christ gave them the victory; then in [Judges 8](/bible/judges/8) Ephraim was upset that they were not called to help in that war. Ephraim always had that leadership attribute, that military spirit.
